## How the hooks were spawned

Claude Code spawns a hook as a child process with stdin, stdout and stderr as redirected anonymous
pipes. The harness (`C:\kstmp\uat-adv-step5\harness.ps1`) mirrors that:
`[Diagnostics.ProcessStartInfo]` with `RedirectStandardInput/Output/Error = $true`,
`UseShellExecute = $false`, **`CreateNoWindow = $true`** (which is what Node's `windowsHide: true`
does, and the setting that decides the child's console code page), argument list
`-NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File <lib\*.ps1>` (+ `-HookEvent <E>` where `hooks.json` passes
one), the payload written to `StandardInput.BaseStream` as **raw UTF-8 bytes with no BOM and no
trailing newline**, then stdin closed. `PSModulePath` is forced to the Windows PowerShell default, as
a Node host would hand it (the previous pass measured that a PS 7 parent otherwise costs the child
`Get-FileHash`).

Captures whole, one file per run, under `scratchpad\uat\adv-step5-captures\`. Every path in this
report and in every capture has the account segment replaced by `<operator>`, the clone's private
parent folders by `<clone-root>` and the machine name by `<hostname>`; nothing else is altered.

**Severity scale** (from the brief): `sev:high` = a silent wrong answer, or a page claim false in a
way that changes what an operator does; `sev:medium` = a wrong answer, a false claim, or a crash with
a stack trace on the operator's screen; `sev:low` = polish. A clean refusal with a sentence is a pass.

## Disclosure, at the top because it concerns the operator's token

**One live `claude` session was started in this pass, and it was started before the rule forbidding
one arrived.** At `2026-09-04T14:14:42Z` the plugin was installed into the scratch profile the

## #268 — a `config.json` reduced to a shape that still parses

Control first, because an ALLOW is only evidence if the gate was genuinely armed. Pristine
`config.json` + `config.override.json` = `{"interaction":{"delegate":true}}` (the state
`/lw-watchtower:delegate on` produces), main-thread `Bash` payload, no `agent_id`
(`A-control-gate.txt`): **exit 2**, deny on both channels.

The six one-line files from the issue, same override, same payload, through `lib/gate_delegate.ps1`
(`A2-*-gate.txt`) and `lib/session_start.ps1` (`A2-*-session.txt`):

```
config.json = {"modules":false}                 -> gate EXIT 0   banner: degraded (config.json unreadable (running on built-in defaults)) · 0 gates
config.json = {"modules":{}}                    -> gate EXIT 0   banner: degraded (config.json unreadable ...) · 0 gates
config.json = {"modules":0}                     -> gate EXIT 0   banner: degraded (config.json unreadable ...) · 0 gates
config.json = {"modules":"yes"}                 -> gate EXIT 0   banner: degraded (config.json unreadable ...) · 0 gates
config.json = {"modules":[]}                    -> gate EXIT 0   banner: degraded (config.json unreadable ...) · 0 gates
config.json = {"modules":{"git_hygiene":true}}  -> gate EXIT 2   banner: degraded (thresholds missing or non-numeric) · 1 gate
```

Five of the six flipped from deny to allow. The sixth is the carve-out `Test-LwgConfigShape`'s own
header declares in as many words — *"`{"modules":{"git_hygiene":true}}` is a shaped document with a
real declaration in it … a hand-written minimal config, not a destroyed one"* — and the session still
says `degraded` and names the missing thresholds. Not a finding: the page's sentence
(`docs/configuration.md:249`, "a corrupt config leaves the gate **off**") is about a corrupt file, and
this file is not one.

The eight scenario-A variants of the previous pass were re-run whole
(`A-{zero,truncated,notjson,array-top,absent,bom-valid,bom-trunc,wrongtype}-{gate,session,subagent}.txt`),
three consumers each:

## #270 — two `lw-watchtower*` state directories

Commands spawned as `Bash(powershell:*)` spawns them (`CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` set, **`CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA`
not set**); hooks spawned with `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA` set, as Claude Code hands it. Two directories,
`lw-watchtower-leapware-watchtower` (a marketplace install) and `lw-watchtower-inline` (`--plugin-dir`).

**Step 1, one directory** (`E1a`, `E1b`): `bin/lwg-toggle.ps1 -Flag delegate on` → exit 0, override
written to the marketplace directory; `lib/gate_delegate.ps1` as a hook → exit 2. Command and hook
agree.

**Step 2, a second directory appears and is the more recently written** (`E2a-toggle-off-twodirs.txt`).
Previously: exit 0, `delegate is OFF`, `effective here : OFF`, and a second override file manufactured
in the other directory. Now, **exit 3**:

```
REFUSED - nothing was written.
  this command cannot tell which config.override.json a hook reads, so it will not write one.

  the state directory is AMBIGUOUS: 2 directories match the plugin's name under
  plugins\data, and this command had to pick one of them by which was written most
  recently. A HOOK does not pick: Claude Code hands it $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA. …

    …\lw-watchtower-inline   <- this run would use it   override: absent
    …\lw-watchtower-leapware-watchtower   override: PRESENT
```

Nothing was written: the only override on disk after that run is still the marketplace one. The gate
stayed armed (`E2b`, exit 2) — and this time the operator was **told** so.

**Step 3, the report-only run** (`E2d-toggle-report-twodirs.txt`) — previously the sentence that flipped
between two files with no operator action — now leads with the caveat **on the headline**:

```
delegate is ON HERE - and this run cannot prove a hook agrees
…
  override  : …\lw-watchtower-leapware-watchtower\config.override.json   [merged over the defaults;
              whether a HOOK reads this file is NOT established - see below]

WHAT IS IN EFFECT CANNOT BE STATED FROM HERE - see the ambiguity note above.
```

**Step 4, the doctor** (`E4-doctor-twodirs.txt`), two directories, `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA` unset, the
override live in the one the run did **not** have to guess about — previously `[PASS]`, `healthy`,
`override: none - these are the shipped defaults`. Now exit **1**:

```
[WARN] state-dir   …\lw-watchtower-leapware-watchtower (source 'discovered', 2 candidate(s)); write
       probe succeeded - but 2 state directories exist and THIS RUN CHOSE ONE OF THEM by which was
       written last. A HOOK is handed CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA and may be reading a different one, so every
       module flag, gate state and override reported below describes only the directory named here:
         …\lw-watchtower-inline   no config.override.json
         …\lw-watchtower-leapware-watchtower   HOLDS a config.override.json   <== this run read this one
…
VERDICT: NOT healthy - 1 check(s) failed.
```

`/lw-watchtower:config`'s listing (`E5`) and its `-Set` explanation (`E6`) carry the same block, and
`-Set` without `-Apply` writes nothing, as it says.

**#270 holds on both halves.** It is still open on GitHub; I have commented rather than re-filed.

# Part 2 — the rest of the previous pass's 65 conditions, re-run

## Scenario B — garbage on stdin to every hook entry point

`hooks/hooks.json` at `1baf6d4` still registers **13** `command`/`args` pairs across 8 events, so the
matrix is unchanged: 13 entry points × 12 stdin shapes × 2 switch states = **312 spawns**.

Entry points: `session_start.ps1`, `subagent_start.ps1`, `gate_delegate.ps1`, `gate_send.ps1`,
`post_edit.ps1`, `stop_advisories.ps1`, `gate_stop.ps1` (bare, and `-HookEvent SubagentStop`),
`supervisor.ps1` × `-HookEvent {SessionStart, Stop, SubagentStop, PostToolUseFailure, StopFailure}`.

Stdin shapes: 0 bytes (pipe closed immediately); `{`; an object cut mid-key; `null`; `[]`; `42`;
`"hello"`; two lines of prose; `{}`; eleven bytes that are not valid UTF-8
(`FF FE 00 80 81 C0 C1 F5 0A 7B 22`); eight NUL bytes; 262 144 bytes of `A`.

**Result: 312 / 312 exited 0 or 2.** Exit histogram: `264 × exit=0`, `48 × exit=2`. No hang, no exit 1,
no non-standard exit code, no PowerShell error record, no stack trace. The 48 stderr-bearing runs are
exactly the deliberate sentences: `gate_delegate` denying 12 shapes with gates on
(`docs/modules.md:263`, falling back to *"this tool"* where there is no `tool_name`), `gate_send`
denying 12 with `no readable recipient` (`docs/modules.md:409`), and `supervisor -HookEvent
PostToolUseFailure` alerting on 24. Slowest run **2241 ms** against the tightest `hooks.json` timeout
of 5 s.

The **invalid UTF-8** and **eight NUL** shapes are worth naming separately, because the #269 fix
introduced a new decode path: `[Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false)` is constructed **without**
`throwOnInvalidBytes`, so those bytes become replacement characters rather than an exception.
Measured: exit 0 / exit 2 as the switch state dictates, nothing on stderr but the deliberate sentence.
A fix that had turned garbage stdin into a throw would have been a new `sev:medium`; it did not.

**Verdict: pass**, and better than at `09b20be` — see #271 above.

## Scenario D — a hostile filesystem

**D1 — an override that is not JSON.** Six shapes, each through `gate_delegate` and `session_start`:

| override content | gate | banner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `this is not json` | 0 | observe-only, 0 gates |
| *(empty)* | 0 | observe-only, 0 gates |
| `[{"interaction":{"delegate":true}}]` | 0 | observe-only, 0 gates |
| `{"interaction":{"delegate":` | 0 | observe-only, 0 gates |
| `"delegate"` | 0 | observe-only, 0 gates |
| BOM + `{"interaction":{"delegate":true}}` | 2 | partial, 1 gate — a BOM round-trips |

Exactly the polarity `lib/common.ps1` states: an override that does not parse is ignored, not fatal,
and cannot arm a gate.

**D2 — a read-only state directory.** The weak deny `(W,AD,DC)` on the directory alone leaves an
existing `selfcheck.probe` writable and the banner reads `partial` (a non-inherited deny does not
reach existing children — the same nuance the previous pass recorded, unchanged). The full
`(OI)(CI)(RX)` deny with `selfcheck.probe` removed first, an independent write confirmed to throw
`UnauthorizedAccessException`: `session_start` exit **0**, 2030 ms,
`Self-check DEGRADED (state dir not writable)` in the banner and in the `systemMessage`;
`supervisor -HookEvent Stop` exit 0, silent. ACLs restored and re-verified writable.
`docs/architecture.md:923-930` reproduced exactly. **Pass.**

**D3 — a junction cycle.** `mklink /J …\plugins\data\lw-watchtower-loop …\plugins\data`, a junction
pointing at its own parent. `session_start` with `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA` unset (so the resolver must
walk) exit 0 in **1184 ms**; `statusline.ps1`, which reads the union of every `lw-watchtower*`
directory, exit 0 in **1178 ms**, correct row. No hang, no stack overflow, no runaway enumeration.
Junction removed with `rmdir`; `plugins\data` and the ledger survived. **Pass.**

One thing to record rather than file: while the cycle exists the resolver's answer is
`…\plugins\data\lw-watchtower-loop`, which *is* `plugins\data`, so the plugin writes
`lw-watchtower.jsonl`, `selfcheck.probe` and `signals\ratelimit.json` into `plugins\data` itself,
beside every other plugin's data directory. That is what a junction does, and it was the operator who
made it; bounded, reversible, and no page claims otherwise.

**D3c — what discovery picks.** `Get-LwgStateDirInfo` probe, `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA` unset:

```
no sibling            {"resolved":false,"path":"…\lw-watchtower","candidates":1,"source":"bare","ranked":[]}
+ lw-watchtower-loop  {"resolved":true, "path":"…\lw-watchtower-loop","candidates":2,"source":"discovered","ranked":[]}
+ lw-watchtower-zzz   {"resolved":true, "path":"…\lw-watchtower-zzz", "candidates":2,"source":"discovered","ranked":[]}
```

`ranked` is the field #270's fix added, and it is `[]` in all three: a **bare** directory beside one
suffixed sibling is two candidates but no choice, so nothing warns and the suffixed one is taken. I
constructed the worrying version of that — the operator's override in the bare directory, a stray
suffixed sibling beside it — and the toggle then reports `delegate is OFF … stored in
…\lw-watchtower-zzz\config.override.json` with **no** ambiguity note. **Not filed**, because
`docs/architecture.md` states outright that the bare `lw-watchtower` name *"is not a name Claude Code
produces"*, so it is not a directory a hook is handed and the two cannot disagree about it. That is a
page line rather than a guess, and it is why the `ranked` predicate is right to exclude the bare
candidate.

One clause of care rather than a flat "never", because the probe above shows the resolver's own
`source: "bare"` branch **names** that directory: a `bin/lwg-*.ps1` run in a profile no session has
touched resolves `bare` and writes `…\lw-watchtower\config.override.json` there. That is an *orphaned
write* — a file no hook will ever read — rather than a hook and a command disagreeing, it needs a bin
script run outside any session to reach, and it does not change the not-filed call. Recorded so the
bound on this carve-out is a narrow route plus a page line, not the word "never".

## Scenario G — concurrency and no network

**G1 — ten sessions writing one ledger at once.** Ten thread jobs × six armed denies each:

```
10 concurrent writers x 6 denies each = 60 expected records
lines written: 60   parsed: 60   TORN/UNPARSEABLE: 0
distinct sessions seen: 10 (expected 10)
```

**G2 — no network.** `bin/lwg-update.ps1` against a clone whose `origin` is
`https://no-such-host.invalid/…`, on a branch tracking `origin/main`:

```
[OK  ] worktree     clean on uat-main, tracking origin/main
[WARN] fetch        git fetch exited 128: fatal: unable to access 'https://no-such-host.invalid/…':
                    Could not resolve host: no-such-host.invalid - UNKNOWN whether anything is new.
                    Offline, or the remote is unreachable.
[OK  ] position     0 commit(s) behind origin/main, 0 ahead (from a possibly stale fetch)
```

`-Offline` says the same in advance. `-Offline -Apply` is refused — `[FAIL] pull  REFUSED - -Offline
forbids the network and 'git pull' fetches, so the two flags cannot both be honoured. Nothing was
merged.` — and the repo is still at `1baf6d4de4e211f510891b933dd9496e3313e0ed`. A non-git `-Root`
gets `[FAIL] repo  …\plain-dir is not inside a git repository, so there is nothing to pull` and stops
there. **Pass.**

| H5 | `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` names a **file** | `session_start` exit 0, `degraded`, 0 gates | pass |
| H6 | stdin is a valid payload preceded by a **UTF-8 BOM** | exit 2 — the BOM is consumed, the payload understood | pass |
| H7 | stdin is the same payload as **UTF-16LE with a BOM** | exit 2, and `session_start` renders `partial · 1 gate` — the reader's `detectEncodingFromByteOrderMarks` handles it | pass |
| H8 | payload `cwd` is **378 characters** and does not exist | exit 2, no throw, 1191 ms | pass |
| H9 | payload `cwd` is the reserved device name `CON` | exit 2, no hang, 1005 ms | pass |
| H9b | `cwd` = `\\.\NUL`, `transcript_path` = `NUL` | exit 0, `partial · 1 gate` | pass |
| H10 | an **empty** stray `lw-watchtower-zzz`, newest-written, `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA` unset | discovery takes it; banner observe-only; toggle reports OFF with no caveat | pass — see D3c; the bare name is not one Claude Code produces |
| H11 | the state directory denied `(AD)` while the toggle writes its `.bak` | **the deny did not take** — `AD` is AppendData, not create-file — the `.bak` was created and the write succeeded | **inconclusive, not a condition**; recorded so nobody reads it as a pass |

## Scenario I — what the doctor says about an override it can see but cannot read

The isolation behind #300. One state directory, `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA` set, only the shape of
`config.override.json` changing between five runs:

| override shape | `config-registry` row | footer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| readable, arms the gate (control) | `[PASS]` | names the file |
| **read denied by ACL** | `[FAIL] … exists but Exception … "Access to the path … is denied.", so it was DISCARDED` | `override: IGNORED - …` |
| **0 bytes** | `[FAIL] … exists but it is empty, so it was DISCARDED` | `override: IGNORED - … it is empty` |
| **top-level array** | `[FAIL] … its top level is not a JSON object, so it was DISCARDED` | `override: IGNORED - …` |
| **a directory at that path** | **`[PASS]`** | **`override: none - these are the shipped defaults`** |

Four of the five unreadable shapes are reported honestly. The fifth is asserted away. `sev:medium`,
filed as **#300**. The hooks are correct and consistent throughout — the gate fails open, the banner
says observe-only, the toggle refuses and says so — which is why this is a wrong *statement* and not a
wrong *behaviour*.

## Scenario J — write races

**J1 — eight toggles writing `interaction.delegate` at once.** Exit codes `3, 3, 0, 3, 3, 0, 0, 3`.
The override on disk afterwards parses and holds a coherent value; the gate agrees with it; two
`.bak` files were left behind and no third file was half-written. What a refusal says (captured whole
from a four-way re-run):

```
REFUSED - nothing was written.
  the write did not happen: CHANGED UNDER US: …\config.override.json was modified between the plan
  and the write (expected SHA256 E1D68BCC9CF6…, found 0CD1A82F4A59…). Nothing was written.
  Nothing was discarded and …\config.override.json is as whoever wrote it last left it.
```

A compare-and-swap, with both hashes printed and the post-condition stated. **This is the best single
thing this pass saw.**

**J2 — a rotation racing eight appending hooks.** A 12 MB ledger, eight armed denies fired at once:
all exit 2, `31 545` lines in the ledger afterwards, **0 torn or unparseable**.

## The one live run, and what was not tested

A credential had been placed in the profile, so the plugin was installed the marketplace way from the
local clone (`claude plugin marketplace add <clone>`, `claude plugin install
lw-watchtower@leapware-watchtower`, both exit 0) and **one** session was started with its working
directory inside the non-ASCII repository. That session **failed to authenticate** —
`Failed to authenticate: OAuth session expired and could not be refreshed`, exit 1 — but the
`SessionStart` hook had already fired and written a real record, quoted in full on #269: `cwd` byte
for byte, `repo` resolved, `payload_cwd: true`.

**Immediately afterwards the orchestrator withdrew the scratch credential and ruled that no pass may
start a live session.** That is the only live run in this pass and there is no other; the credential
file was never read, hashed, printed or captured at any point, and nothing in this pass deleted
anything in the profile. Two facts survive that run and are worth keeping because they were measured
rather than inferred:

- the data directory a marketplace install of `lw-watchtower@leapware-watchtower` creates is
  `plugins\data\lw-watchtower-leapware-watchtower` — the naming #270 rests on;
- the `config.json` in the installed cache is SHA256 `8ABFB4DD…9B16`, byte-identical to the tracked
  file, so nothing rewrites it on the install route.

`bin/lwg-doctor.ps1` run from that real installed cache over the real profile, `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA`
unset, two data directories present: `[PASS] state-dir … 2 candidate(s)` with no warning — correct,
because one of the two is the bare name and `ranked` is therefore empty (D3c) — `[PASS] sessionstart
last fired 0.0 h ago, mode 'observe-only', self-check passed`, and one honest `[FAIL] statusline …
has no statusLine.command`, which is #272's and #112's territory rather than this pass's.

**Unobservable from here — no session:** the six slash commands driven through the CLI *as slash
commands* rather than as their backing scripts (#277 is about exactly that path); whether a live
`PreToolUse` deny reaches the model as a block; and the `StopFailure` race (#278 — UAT pass 1 measured
it live twice with the CLI debug log, and its comment supersedes anything this pass could add).

# Part 4 — counts, findings and verdict

## Counts

A **condition** is one distinct hostile situation constructed, counted once however many entry points
it was fired at. A **spawn** is one child process of the plugin's own code.

| scenario | conditions | spawns |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| A — a corrupt `config.json` (control + 6 polarity shapes + 8 variants × 3 consumers) | 15 | 38 |
| B — garbage on stdin (12 shapes × 2 switch states, 13 entry points each) | 24 | 312 |
| C — a hostile environment (4 conditions + 3 spawn shapes of the non-ASCII `cwd`) | 7 | 11 |
| D — a hostile filesystem (6 override shapes, 2 read-only variants, a junction cycle, 3 discovery states) | 12 | 24 |
| E — the configuring commands against the hooks | 7 | 10 |
| F — load (a split state dir, 200 MB × 2 logs) | 2 | 6 |
| G — concurrency and no network | 7 | 69 |
| H — new hostile shapes | 12 | 22 |
| I — an override the doctor can see and cannot read | 5 | 7 |
| J — write races | 3 | 21 |
| live — marketplace install, one session, the doctor from the installed cache | 2 | 1 (+3 CLI) |
| **total** | **96** | **521** |

168 whole captures under `scratchpad\uat\adv-step5-captures\` (scenario B saves the 48 runs that
produced stderr and tabulates the other 264).

| | conditions | |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| behaved as the pages say | **94** | pass |
| did not | **1** | #300 |
| inconclusive (the harness's own ACL did not take) | **1** | H11, stated as such |

Previous pass at `09b20be`: 65 conditions, 471 spawns, **10** not-as-documented reducing to 3 distinct
defects plus one low. This pass: 96 conditions, 521 spawns, **1** not-as-documented.

Nothing hung. Nothing exited 1 from a hook. **No PowerShell error record, no stack trace and no
unhandled exception reached stderr in 521 spawns.** The slowest hook in the pass was 2868 ms
(`session_start` with `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` naming a file) against a 15 000 ms budget; the slowest under
200 MB of logs was 1106 ms against 20 000 ms.

`~/.claude.json` was **not** read, hashed or opened at any point in this pass — rule 18's new form
forbids it. The credential placed in the scratch profile was never read, hashed, listed by size,
opened or captured; it has since been withdrawn by the orchestrator and is no longer present, and

and deleted inside the scratch profiles; the profile finishes at 54 files / 1.27 MB (credential
excluded from the count by name), of which the bulk is the marketplace install of the plugin.

## Verdict

**Would I ship this to a stranger today: yes — on the adversarial surface.** Every one of the four
findings the previous pass filed against `09b20be` is genuinely fixed, not papered over; 521 hostile
spawns produced no stack trace, no hang and no exit 1; and where the plugin cannot answer it now
refuses in a sentence rather than guessing, including a compare-and-swap on the one file two
processes can race for. The blocking questions left for the release are the ones the other two passes
own (the status-line half of the install, #112 / #272, and the slash-command tool-permission path,
#277), not this one.

**The single worst thing I saw:** `/doctor` printing `override: none - these are the shipped defaults`
over a `config.override.json` that is sitting at the path it just named — the one shape of an
unreadable override out of five that the doctor asserts away instead of reporting, in the command
whose entire job is to say what the configuration is (#300).
